first_impression.reaction: OK, this is what I googled. The second sentence tells me the ideas are grouped by style, so I know I can scroll to the bit I like. The title reads a bit clunky though, 'Place Cards Ideas', like it was written for Google and not for me. Key takeaways are useful, but they're all about logistics, not the ideas I came for.

journey.quote: These wedding place cards ideas are grouped by style, so you can shortlist in a minute: classic paper, natural and edible, keepsakes, glass and acrylic, local touches, and cards that sit on the napkin or plate.
journey.reaction: Good, straight to it and it tells me the map of the page. 'Place cards ideas' sounds off though.

journey.quote: Choose a place card style that suits the setting first, then check it can stand up to wind, heat and travel.
journey.reaction: Sensible, but I came for ideas and none of the takeaways actually names one. I'd want the styles summed up here so I can screenshot it on the train.

journey.quote: Take every name from one source, your finished seating plan, and check spelling, titles and preferred names before anything is made.
journey.reaction: Fair point, my cousin's place card had her ex's surname on it. Useful.

journey.quote: An escort card waits near the entrance and tells a guest which table they are at; a place card sits on the table and marks the exact seat.
journey.reaction: One sentence, cleared up something I was half confused about. Nice.

journey.quote: Leaves curl in heat, so letter them close to the day and keep them cool.
journey.reaction: This is the kind of practical tip I wouldn't think of, especially in Singapore humidity. Each idea is short and has a 'watch out' attached. I'd skim this section and bookmark.

journey.quote: This is general information rather than legal advice, and for a wedding overseas, ask the venue how its kitchen handles allergens.
journey.reaction: Whole paragraph about the Food Standards Code and legal advice for a macaron with a name on it. Feels heavy and Australia-specific for someone reading on their phone. The takeaway bullet already said it more simply.

journey.section: Glass, Mirror and Acrylic Place Cards
journey.quote: Clear acrylic disappears against white linen, so a tinted or frosted finish, or a contrasting lettering colour, keeps the name readable.
journey.reaction: Acrylic is what I was leaning towards, and I hadn't thought of this. Gained a point.

journey.section: How to Do Wedding Place Cards
journey.quote: Order or make the cards once RSVPs have closed and the seating plan is settled.
journey.reaction: Clear answer to my next question. But nothing about how much any of this costs or whether DIY is cheaper.

journey.quote: Wedding name cards can be as simple as that.
journey.reaction: Odd tacked-on line, reads like it's there for search, not for me.

unanswered_questions: Roughly how much do place cards cost, and is DIY cheaper than ordering from a stationer?
When was this written or last updated? Is it current for 2026?
How far ahead of the wedding should I contact a stationer so they have time to make them?
The link said '25 unique place cards' but I count 21 ideas on the page. Did I miss some?

turn_offs_found.quote: Wedding Place Cards Ideas for Every Table
turn_offs_found.why: Clunky grammar in the headline makes it look keyword-stuffed, which makes me trust it a bit less before I start.

turn_offs_found.quote: A food allergy reaction can include anaphylaxis, and in Australia the Food Standards Code requires certain foods and substances to be declared when they are present as ingredients.
turn_offs_found.why: Too legal and too long for an ideas post on my phone. I'm not in Australia and I just want to know to tell my caterer.

would_share_with: My fiance, for the acrylic and fruit ideas
My maid of honour, who is helping with the table styling

cta_reaction.quote: If you would like someone to manage the guest list and the vendor briefings with you, start a conversation with Wedded Concierge.
cta_reaction.why: I only wanted place card ideas and I don't know this brand. I might tap the stationer directory or the seating app link because they answer my next question, but talking to a planner is a big jump from a place card search.
